from.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison before the inverse limit: Infinity-categorical monadicity and the augmented counit bar resolution. Supporting foundation: Free coherent monad modules and their augmented free resolution. Supporting lemma: Underlying equivalences and operadic colimits of coherent modules. Supporting step: Coherent modules as inert-preserving simplicial sections.

title: Coherent modules as inert-preserving simplicial sections
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and sufficiently large universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], monoidal infinity-categories of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and inner and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $\mathcal V$ be monoidal, $\mathcal M$ coherently left-tensored over $\mathcal V$, and $B$ an associative algebra in $\mathcal V$; these structures include all higher associativity and unit compatibilities, with the operadic encoding of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. Write $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ for objects of $\mathcal M$ with coherent unital associative $B$-action, retaining action-preserving maps and all higher simplices, and $U$ for the underlying-object functor. There is a categorical fibration
$$q_B:X_B\longrightarrow N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$$
with the following properties. Categorical fibration means inner fibration with lifting of equivalence edges with specified source. It is locally cocartesian: pulling it back along any edge $\Delta^1\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ gives a cocartesian fibration. Its fiber at $[n]$ is equivalent to $\mathcal M$. If $\beta:[n]\to[m]$ is opposite to $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ in $\Delta$, its local transport, under these fiber identifications, is
$$\beta_!(x)\simeq B^{\otimes(n-\alpha(m))}\otimes x,$$
where the zeroth power acts as the identity via the unit constraint. For $x\in(X_B)_{[n]}$ and $y\in(X_B)_{[m]}$, the space of arrows over $\beta$ is naturally $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(\beta_!x,y)$; locally cocartesian arrows correspond to equivalences in this description.

Let $\Gamma(q_B)=\operatorname{Fun}_{N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})}(N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}),X_B)$ denote coherent sections and transformations whose image in the base is the identity transformation, with their higher simplices over the identity. Let $I$ consist of the arrows opposite to interval inclusions $\alpha:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$ with $\alpha(m)=n$. Then there is an equivalence
$$\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)\simeq\Gamma_I(q_B)\subseteq\Gamma(q_B),$$
where $\Gamma_I(q_B)$ is the full subcategory of sections carrying every edge of $I$ to a locally cocartesian edge. Under this equivalence evaluation at every $[n]$, followed by the fiber equivalence with $\mathcal M$, is naturally equivalent to $U$. These equivalences are supplied by the section edges opposite to $[0]\to[n]$, $0\mapsto n$. No colimit, limit or presentability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Corollary 4.2.2.16, Notation 4.2.2.17, Remarks 4.2.2.18-19, Lemma 4.2.2.20 and Remark 4.2.2.21 and condition (2') in Remark 4.2.2.19, printed pp. 518-519. Condition (2') there asks the inert edges with alpha(m)=n to be (p∘q)-coCartesian; its equivalence with the locally coCartesian condition defining Gamma_I here follows from Remark 4.2.2.22 (p. 519-520: composites with these edges preserve local coCartesianness), the dual of Higher Topos Theory (2009) Lemma 2.4.2.7, and HTT Proposition 2.4.1.3, since the algebra section carries these edges to coCartesian edges. The identification of each evaluation with the forgetful functor is also stated at the end of the proof of HA Proposition 4.2.3.4 (p. 528). Online source read; WANTED: archived Higher Algebra in literature/. No Stacks tag covers this coherent module model.

proof.text: Represent the given action by the cocartesian operadic fibration $r:\mathcal O\to L$ of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. Let $D=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ and use the explicit functors $\mathrm{Cut}$, $\mathrm{LCut}$ and the transformation $\gamma$ of [lem-coef-lm-prism-approximation]. Write $b=B\mathrm{Cut}:D\to\mathcal O$. Construct $X_B$ as follows: a $k$-simplex is a map $\sigma:\Delta^k\to D$ and a lift $h:\Delta^k\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal O$ of $\gamma(\sigma\times1)$ with top restriction $b\sigma$, all of whose vertex arrows over $\theta_n$ are inert. Operators restrict both maps. Thus $X_B$ is the full subcategory, on these inert arrows, of the degreewise pullback of the relative endpoint-$1$ corner map for $r$. This constructs the object and all its higher simplices; it is not a choice of data from an existence theorem.

source.place: Notation 4.2.2.17, fixed-algebra pullback (online, not archived; the argument is expanded here)

proof.text: The relative endpoint-$1$ corner map is a categorical fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], with the inclusion $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$; $r$ is a categorical fibration by its operadic definition. Pulling back its horn and equivalence lifting problems gives the same lifting properties for the unrestricted prism object over $D$. Restricting to the full subcategory in step 1 preserves them: an inner-horn filler has the same vertices, and an equivalence lift stays among inert vertex arrows. For the latter assertion, a square of arrows which is an equivalence in the arrow category has equivalences on both endpoints by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], so it preserves the homotopy-pullback test for an $r$-cocartesian arrow in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. Composition with these endpoint equivalences induces inverse maps up to the inverse-triangle homotopies, using [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], so the pullback test is unchanged. The base vertical arrow remains $\theta_n$. Consequently $q_B:X_B\to D$ is the required categorical fibration.

source.place: Remark 4.2.2.19; explicit endpoint-corner and full-subcategory argument (online, not archived; the argument is expanded here)

proof.text: At $[n]$ a vertex is an inert projection from a mixed tuple to the pure tuple $b([n])$. Under the Segal equivalences in [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding], it has source $(B,\ldots,B,x)$ and target $(B,\ldots,B)$, with its algebra coordinates identified by equivalences, and the projection discards $x$. To obtain the last-colour projection as a coherent functor, let $K=(X_B)_{[n]}$ and let $a_n:K\to\mathcal O$ evaluate each prism at its bottom endpoint. Its base is constant at $w=(\langle n+1\rangle,\{n+1\})$. The inert projection $\rho_m:w\to m$ gives a constant transformation from $ra_n$ to the constant diagram at $m$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] with this $K$, this diagram and this transformation. Its lifted target is a functor $e_n:K\to\mathcal O_m=\mathcal M$ and its vertex maps are precisely inert last-colour projections. Thus the fibre identification is defined on all coherent transformations and higher simplices, not just objects. For every $x$, take the mixed tuple with these algebra coordinates and use an $r$-cocartesian lift of $\theta_n$; its target is equivalent to $b([n])$ by the pure Segal equivalence, so composing with that equivalence gives a vertex of the stated strict fibre. On mapping spaces the output product decomposition says that a commuting square between two such projections consists of the prescribed algebra-coordinate comparisons and one arbitrary map $x\to y$. The space of the former comparisons with their specified identifications is contractible. More explicitly it is the homotopy fibre of an equivalence on those factors. The mapping-space formula for cocartesian lifts in [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport], at $K=\Delta^0$, identifies this with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(x,y)$. Thus $e_n$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image]: its replete essential image is all of $\mathcal M$, so it supplies a coherent quasi-inverse and the asserted fibre equivalence. For $n=0$ the pure tuple is empty and its fibre is terminal; the product of algebra-coordinate comparison spaces is a point, leaving exactly $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(x,y)$.

source.place: Remark 4.2.2.18; mixed-tuple Segal decomposition and inert projection (online, not archived; the argument is expanded here)

proof.text: Fix $\beta=\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}:[n]\to[m]$. Its $\mathrm{LCut}$ map partitions the algebra inputs into the $m$ blocks $(\alpha(j-1),\alpha(j)]$, discards the prefix through $\alpha(0)$, and puts precisely the tail $(\alpha(m),n]$ together with $x$ in the module output. In a square defining an arrow of $X_B$ over $\beta$, the pure-algebra output maps are fixed to be those of $b(\beta)$. Apply the operadic mapping-space product decomposition: taking the fibre over those fixed algebra maps removes exactly the pure-algebra factors, leaving the space of module operations from that tail and $x$ to $y$. Take the $r$-cocartesian lift of the ordered tail operation. The cocartesian mapping-space fibre formula [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport], at $K=\Delta^0$, identifies this last space naturally with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(B^{\otimes(n-\alpha(m))}\otimes x,y)$. All these decompositions are induced by projections and composition, so the equality of fibres is natural on the full mapping spaces and higher simplices, not only on components. The module identity at this tensor object, together with the fixed algebra block maps, supplies an arrow over $\beta$. In the pullback over $\Delta^1$, precomposition by this arrow is the identity on the just-displayed mapping spaces into objects of the target fibre; into objects of the source fibre it is a square with empty bottom left corner. It therefore passes the homotopy-pullback criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. The edge pullback is a cocartesian fibration, with the displayed transport. For an arbitrary arrow, let $u:t\to y$ be its remaining module map, where $t=B^{\otimes(n-\alpha(m))}\otimes x$. The criterion says precisely that precomposition $\operatorname{Map}(y,z)\to\operatorname{Map}(t,z)$ is an equivalence for every $z$. If $u$ is invertible, its inverse gives the inverse precomposition maps. Conversely the bijection on components at $z=t$ gives $v:y\to t$ with $vu=1_t$; injectivity at $z=y$ then gives $uv=1_y$, since $(uv)u=u=1_yu$. The homotopy-category and inverse-edge criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] makes $u$ an equivalence. This proves exactly the asserted characterization of locally cocartesian arrows. The exponent is nonnegative because $\alpha(m)\leq n$, and the empty tail is the identity action by the unit constraint.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2.20 and Remark 4.2.2.21; explicit ordered-block mapping-space computation (online, not archived; the argument is expanded here)

proof.text: A coherent section of $q_B$, including transformations and higher simplices over $D$, is exactly a prism lift $F:D\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal O$ over $\gamma$, with fixed top $b$ and inert vertical edges: this is the degreewise exponential adjunction applied to step 1. If $\alpha:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$ is an interval inclusion ending at $n$, the algebra blocks each have one input and the module tail is empty. The algebra section $B$ carries the pure inert map to an inert arrow. Consequently the Segal projections make the mixed bottom edge inert exactly when its module comparison $x\to y$ is an equivalence: after inert transport the algebra comparisons are already equivalences, and the remaining comparison is the module map, by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. Step 4 identifies precisely that condition with local $q_B$-cocartesianness. Thus the bottom inert condition is exactly the condition defining $\Gamma_I(q_B)$. The marking classification of [lem-coef-lm-prism-approximation] exhausts the other marked edges: top ones are already inert because $B$ is an algebra, vertical ones are imposed by construction, and a marked cross edge factors through an inert vertical and an inert top edge. Their composite is inert by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], applied to $r$ and the corresponding prism triangle. Therefore $\Gamma_I(q_B)$ is exactly the category of lifts sending every $\gamma$-marked edge to an inert arrow and having fixed top $b$. This comparison checks the inert operadic condition directly; it assumes no global cocartesian condition on $q_B$.

source.place: Definition 4.2.2.10, Proposition 4.2.2.12, Corollary 4.2.2.16 and Remark 4.2.2.19; direct comparison of inert bottom edges (online, not archived; the argument is expanded here)

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction] twice: to $\gamma:D\times\Delta^1\to L$ and $r:\mathcal O\to L$, and to $\mathrm{Cut}:D\to A$ and its pure-algebra restriction $r|_A$. All its hypotheses are supplied by [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding] and [lem-coef-lm-prism-approximation]: these are operadic fibrations, the two maps are approximations, and their colour fibres are equivalences. This gives a commutative square whose horizontal maps are equivalences, from inert-preserving sections over $L$ to marked prism lifts, and from algebra sections over $A$ to inert-preserving lifts of $\mathrm{Cut}$. The vertical maps are restriction to $A$ and to the top face. They are categorical fibrations: apply the relative corner-map theorem [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to the inclusions $A\hookrightarrow L$ and $D\times\{1\}\hookrightarrow D\times\Delta^1$, with target $r$. Pull back along the specified base functors, and restrict to the full subcategories of inert-preserving objects. Inner horn fillers have unchanged vertices; equivalence lifts remain in these subcategories because equivalences of diagrams are componentwise by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] and the mapping-square criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] is invariant under endpoint equivalences (the inverse and homotopies are those of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], as in step 2). For the prism restriction, the top marking is the restriction of the full marking, so these corner lifts have the required target. Now [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] identifies each strict fibre, at $B$ on the left and $b=B\mathrm{Cut}$ on the right, with the corresponding pullback in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. The square of horizontal equivalences induces an equivalence of these pullbacks: for any test quasicategory the displayed homotopy-pullback formula of that lemma is unchanged under the two equivalences. The left fibre is $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ by definition, and the right fibre is $\Gamma_I(q_B)$ by step 5. We have obtained the required equivalence, retaining transformations and all higher simplices. Its functor is restriction, so its value at $([0],0)$ is the original section's value at $m$.

source.place: Definition 2.3.3.6, Theorems 2.3.3.23 and 2.3.3.26 applied to Remark 4.2.2.8 and Proposition 4.1.2.11; fixed-algebra comparison of Corollary 4.2.2.16. Explicit strict-fibre versus homotopy-fibre argument written by the agent.

proof.text: For $[n]$ use the opposite of the interval inclusion $[0]\hookrightarrow[n]$ selecting $n$. It belongs to $I$, and its transport is the identity on the module fibre by the empty-tail calculation. Every section in $\Gamma_I(q_B)$ consequently gives an equivalence $e_n(s([n]))\simeq e_0(s([0]))$. Evaluation of a coherent transformation of sections on this fixed base edge gives its naturality square, and evaluation of higher simplices gives all higher compatibilities. Under the restriction equivalence proved in step 6, evaluation at $([0],0)$ is the value of the operadic section at $m$, which is $U$ by [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. The componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes this a coherent natural equivalence. Composing gives the requested natural equivalence between every evaluation and $U$. At $n=0$ it is the identity. All preceding constructions used only the specified operadic tensoring, its mapping spaces and categorical-fibration lifting; no existence or preservation of colimits, limits or presentability was invoked.

split_report.summary: Seven-step proof: explicitly construct the fixed-algebra inert-prism object, prove categorical lifting, compute its fibres and ordered-tail mapping spaces, identify marked bottom edges with the required locally cocartesian edges, apply the general approximation theorem twice and pass to fixed-algebra fibres, then compare evaluations. Three statement-only dependencies specify the LM operadic encoding, the general approximation restriction theorem, and the combinatorial Cut/prism approximations. The last two are separated so no new node merely repeats the module-section equivalence. No mathematical statement change, Lean or build. Second reading constructs the coherent fibre projection using the existing pointwise transport theorem with the entire fibre as diagram shape.
